The performance in 2017 has been impacted by the worst year for catastrophes in the US for over a decade with Hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria, the wildfires in California and earthquakes in Mexico causing insured market losses of $135 billion the costliest year on record. The impact of the catastrophe losses on Syndicate 1910 net of reinsurance recoveries added 18.16 percentage points to the combined ratio. The net impact of these events was managed due to the effectiveness of the reinsurance programme purchased to protect against such large events. The losses mainly impacted the 2017 Year of Account and as such the expected result on this year of account will be disappointing compared to prior years with fewer catastrophes.

gpt-5-mini.standardized_narrative: The syndicate opened the year with gross claims outstanding of GBP 180.1m. Management reports a net favourable development (a surplus) on prior years of GBP 38.5m in 2017, driven by favourable claims development across prior underwriting years. Current-year catastrophe activity (Hurricanes Harvey, Irma, Maria, California wildfires and Mexican earthquakes) materially impacted the 2017 underwriting year net of reinsurance but the prior-year position overall showed a release. The release represents approximately a 21.4% reduction relative to opening gross claims outstanding.

gpt-5-mini.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding is taken from Note 3 Technical provisions (explicit). Prior year development amount is taken from the statement 'In 2017 the surplus was GBP 38.5m.' in the claims development narrative and interpreted as a release (negative sign) per Lloyd's surplus/deficit convention. No explicit 'Movement in prior year's provision' aggregate line was present; the claims development triangle was partially formatted and ambiguous, so the single explicit 'surplus' sentence was used. Some named event impacts on reserves are described qualitatively; event-level financial impacts to the syndicate are not quantified in the report.
